$comment: Pinch's capability inventory. Every entry claims evidence — a file or symbol a reader can open. The market researcher (scripts/market.js) refuses to credit a capability it cannot prove, and refuses to call one missing unless the claim is genuinely absent. Update this file when a capability lands or dies; a stale inventory makes every comparison wrong in the flattering direction.

capabilities.name: Reachable from the chat apps a person already uses
Accepts screenshots, documents and files
evidence: src/server.js: multipart handling for voice notes
capabilities.note: Voice notes are handled; arbitrary documents are not turned into context.

capabilities.name: Understands images with a vision model
Plugs into MCP servers for third-party tools
evidence: no mcp reference anywhere in src/
capabilities.note: The emerging interoperability standard. Its absence is the biggest structural gap against every competitor in this list.

capabilities.name: A documented way to add tools without editing core files
evidence: src/tools.js: tools are a fixed list in this file
capabilities.note: Adding a tool means editing src/tools.js. That is fine for one maintainer and a wall for anybody else.

capabilities.name: Indexes your documents and answers from them
evidence: search_web is network-only; there is no embedding store

capabilities.name: An agent that runs a task on a schedule without you
evidence: src/scheduler.js: reminders fire, but they do not run tools

capabilities.name: Talk to it and have it read replies back
evidence: docs/GUIDE.md: voice needs a whisper server; wake word needs an open tab
capabilities.note: Input works with a configured whisper endpoint. Nothing here is offline out of the box.

capabilities.name: Looks things up on the web
Separate accounts and permissions for several people
evidence: PINCH_KEY is one shared secret; there is no user table
capabilities.note: Deliberately out of scope: one person, one laptop. Not a gap to close, a boundary to keep.

capabilities.name: Optional cloud model when the user configures one
Runs a local model with no cloud account
evidence: src/brain.js: ollama provider is the default
capabilities.note: The identity of the product. Everything else is optional on top.

capabilities.name: A native phone app
evidence: public/index.html is installable as a PWA
capabilities.note: A PWA that installs from the browser. Cheaper than an app and enough for one person.

capabilities.name: Executes commands and edits files, with approval
evidence: src/tools.js: shell, read_file, write_file, list_dir, grep

$policy: Every capability carries a policy. 'in-scope' may be proposed. 'settled' has been decided and is only shown so the decision is visible. 'out-of-scope' contradicts the product identity in .github/prompts/self-improvement.md; the researcher reports it and the proposer is forbidden from acting on it.
